title: Size, structure and resources of each economy

research.summary:
Gathered all requested size, structure and resource measures for the 13 World Bank-covered economies (USA, CHN, EU27=EUU, DEU, JPN, IND, GBR, RUS, CAN, MEX, KOR, SAU, BRA), plus Taiwan and the world (WLD). 2024 is the common year throughout. Main source: World Bank WDI API (lastupdated 2026-10-08), 18 series fetched for all 14 codes for 2010-2025.

Taiwan: GDP (US$801.5 bn), PPP GDP and population come from IMF WEO October 2026 via DataMapper. Labor force (12,001 thousand), value-added shares and trade shares come from DGBAS national statistics (official xlsx). Military spending comes from SIPRI v1.2. General government spending comes from IMF Fiscal Monitor October 2026. Energy dependence comes from the Energy Administration (MOEA) open API.

General government expenditure: IMF Fiscal Monitor (Oct 2026) for 13 economies; Eurostat gov_10a_main for EU27 (48.9%).

EU27 as a bloc: WDI trade shares (exports 50.4%, imports 46.1%) INCLUDE intra-EU trade. Extra-EU trade comes from Eurostat bop_eu6_q (BPM6): exports EUR 4,182 bn = 23.1% of GDP, imports EUR 3,648 bn = 20.1%; converted to US$ at ECB 1.0824.

Caveats and fallbacks:
(1) WDI natural resource rents and oil rents end in 2021 for every economy, so those rows are 2021.
(2) WDI US value-added shares stop at 2021 (older BEA vintage). US 2024 shares were computed from OECD SDMX table T0101 (BEA data): VA at basic prices / GDP at market prices; agriculture 0.94, industry 17.34, manufacturing 9.88, services 78.27.
(3) Canada value-added shares are 2022, the latest anywhere. Statistics Canada table 36-10-0711 has current-dollar industry values only to 2022 (2023-2025 not available; checked via its WDS API), and OECD 2022 equals WDI.
(4) EUU energy imports net is 2023 (2024 not in WDI). Eurostat import dependency for 2024 is added under its own definition (EU27 57.3%, DEU 66.8%).
(5) WDI military series are SIPRI's. Values were checked identical to the SIPRI v1.2 workbook, and EUU 2024 equals the sum of the 27 members (US$360,219.1 m). US figures are for the fiscal year; Saudi Arabia includes security and the Ministry of Interior; China is a SIPRI estimate above the official budget. World military spending: WDI sum of countries US$2.667 tn vs SIPRI world total US$2.692 tn (includes SIPRI's estimates for gaps).
(6) Value-added shares are VA at basic prices over GDP at market prices, so they do not sum to 100.
(7) Taiwan: services were computed from sections G-S, because the DGBAS addendum 'Services' line includes import duties and VAT. Taiwan's PPP is the IMF's (the World Bank publishes none), so use the IMF world totals included here for shares. DGBAS gives Taiwan GDP of US$801.529 bn vs IMF 801.495 bn. Taiwan resource rents, oil rents and WDI-concept net energy imports are null with reasons. Taiwan's official 'dependence on imported energy' (95.14%) counts nuclear as imported, so it is given as a separately named measure.
(8) Labor force is the ILO modelled estimate (WDI); Taiwan's is DGBAS civilian.
(9) WDI already has 2025 values for GDP, PPP, population, labor force and military, but 2025 trade is missing for USA and JPN, so 2024 was kept.

What failed:
- IMF DataMapper returned 403 Access Denied for User-Agent 'why-2-research/0.1'; it works with 'why-2-global/0.1 (https://github.com/atonalfreerider/why-2)' (the project's form) or curl's default.
- DataMapper ignores country and period filters (full download; only extracts were saved).
- DataMapper's BX_GDP/BM_GDP are Africa REO only; NGDP is not in DataMapper.
- The first multi-country WB call timed out once; the retry worked.
- StatCan WDS served its maintenance page after a 104-coordinate batch (later recovered). Its provincial tables have no Canada total.
- EIA's Taiwan page is JS-rendered with no text; the Energy Administration's English statistics menu is empty, so its open API was used instead.
- Eurostat bop_c6_a has no EU27 reporter, so bop_eu6_q was used.

Files (all under /home/john/Desktop/Unity/.why-2-build/research/global/size-structure-resources/):
- raw/wb, raw/imf (extracts), raw/taiwan, raw/other/{sipri,oecd,eurostat,statcan}
- scripts/ (fetch_wb.py, fetch_imf.py, fetch_statcan.py, sipri_extract.py, xlsx_dump_lib.py, jsonstat.py, build_rows.py)
- rows.json: the same rows as returned here, with full-length notes.
The 922 KB SIPRI workbook was deleted after extracting raw/other/sipri/sipri_milex_extract.json. No events were in scope for this domain.

research.fetch_recipe:
Run all parsing with python3 -I. Rebuild everything offline from the saved raw files with: python3 -I scripts/build_rows.py <research_dir>. Research dir: /home/john/Desktop/Unity/.why-2-build/research/global/size-structure-resources

1) World Bank WDI (no key)
GET https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/USA;CHN;EUU;DEU;JPN;IND;GBR;RUS;CAN;MEX;KOR;SAU;BRA;WLD/indicator/{CODE}?format=json&date=2010:2025&per_page=1000
- Codes: NY.GDP.MKTP.CD, NY.GDP.MKTP.PP.CD, SP.POP.TOTL, SL.TLF.TOTL.IN, NV.AGR.TOTL.ZS, NV.IND.TOTL.ZS, NV.IND.MANF.ZS, NV.SRV.TOTL.ZS, NE.EXP.GNFS.ZS, NE.IMP.GNFS.ZS, NE.EXP.GNFS.CD, NE.IMP.GNFS.CD, NY.GDP.TOTL.RT.ZS, NY.GDP.PETR.RT.ZS, NY.GDP.NGAS.RT.ZS, EG.IMP.CONS.ZS, MS.MIL.XPND.CD, MS.MIL.XPND.GD.ZS.
- Response is [meta, rows]. Use row.countryiso3code, int(row.date), row.value. Take 2024, else 2023, else the latest non-null year. meta.lastupdated is 2026-10-08.
- Indicator metadata: https://api.worldbank.org/v2/indicator/{CODE}?format=json
- Script: scripts/fetch_wb.py. Use 150 s timeouts and retries (one call timed out).

2) IMF DataMapper (no key)
GET https://www.imf.org/external/datamapper/api/v1/{NGDPD|PPPGDP|LP|G_X_G01_GDP_PT}
- Returns every country and year; path and ?periods filters are ignored.
- Parse values[IND][ISO3 or group][year]. NGDPD/PPPGDP are in billions, LP in millions. World = WEOWORLD; euro area = EURO; the Fiscal Monitor has no EU27.
- Vintage from https://www.imf.org/external/datamapper/api/v1/indicators (WEO October 2026, Fiscal Monitor October 2026).
- Akamai returns 403 for User-Agent 'why-2-research/0.1'. Use 'why-2-global/0.1 (https://github.com/atonalfreerider/why-2)' or curl's default.
- Script: scripts/fetch_imf.py (saves extracts).

3) OECD SDMX (US value added by activity)
GET https://sdmx.oecd.org/public/rest/data/OECD.SDD.NAD,DSD_NAMAIN10@DF_TABLE1_OUTPUT,/A.USA+CAN........V..?startPeriod=2021&format=csvfilewithlabels
- Key order: FREQ.REF_AREA.SECTOR.COUNTERPART_SECTOR.TRANSACTION.INSTR_ASSET.ACTIVITY.EXPENDITURE.UNIT_MEASURE.PRICE_BASE.TRANSFORMATION.TABLE_IDENTIFIER
- Keep UNIT_MEASURE=XDC (UNIT_MULT 6). Use TRANSACTION B1GQ (GDP) and B1G with ACTIVITY A, BTE, C, F, GTI, J, K, L, M_N, OTQ, RTU, _T.
- Shares: industry = (BTE+F)/B1GQ; services = (GTI+J+K+L+M_N+OTQ+RTU)/B1GQ.

4) Eurostat (JSON-stat 2.0; flatten in dimension index order; scripts/jsonstat.py)
Base: https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/api/dissemination/statistics/1.0/data/
- bop_eu6_q?format=JSON&lang=EN&geo=EU27_2020&partner=EXT_EU27_2020&bop_item=GS&currency=MIO_EUR&sector10=S1&sectpart=S1&stk_flow=CRE&stk_flow=DEB&s_adj=NSA&sinceTimePeriod=2023-Q1 (contains freq=A rows; bop_c6_a has no EU27 reporter)
- nama_10_gdp?...&geo=EU27_2020&na_item=B1GQ&unit=CP_MEUR
- gov_10a_main?...&na_item=TE&sector=S13&unit=PC_GDP
- nrg_ind_id?...&siec=TOTAL&unit=PC
- ert_bil_eur_a?...&currency=USD&statinfo=AVG

5) SIPRI
GET https://www.sipri.org/sites/default/files/SIPRI-Milex-data-1949-2025_v1.2.xlsx (922 KB; the link is on https://www.sipri.org/databases/milex)
- Sheets: 'Current US$' (US$ m), 'Share of GDP' (fraction), 'Local currency calendar years', 'Regional totals' (US$ bn, constant 2024 prices).
- The header row starts with 'Country'; year columns follow. Parse with zipfile+XML (scripts/xlsx_dump_lib.py, scripts/sipri_extract.py).

6) Taiwan
DGBAS file names change with each release (056, 060a), so re-scrape the pages for current links:
- https://eng.stat.gov.tw/cp.aspx?n=2334 (National Accounts tables)
- https://eng.stat.gov.tw/cp.aspx?n=4212 (Key Economic and Social Indicators: index-eng.xlsx)
- Labor press list https://eng.stat.gov.tw/News.aspx?n=2369&sms=10854&page=2&PageSize=20, then the 'Manpower Survey Results in December 2024' page and its Table 1 xlsx.
Parsing:
- Activity xlsx, sheet 'Gross Domestic Product ': wide; find the 2024 column from the header row. Rows 'A. ...' to 'S. ...' plus 'GDP'. Industry = B-F; services = sections G-S. The addendum 'Services' line includes import duties and VAT.
- Expenditure xlsx, sheet 'GDP(nominal,1981～)': column 2 = year, 34 = exports, 37 = imports, 42 = GDP (million NT$).
- Manpower Table 1: row 'AVE., 2024', column 2 = labor force (thousands).
Energy Administration open API (no key; Swagger at https://ea01.moeaea.gov.tw/a0303/02/api/pages/database/api):
- https://ea01.moeaea.gov.tw/a0303/02/api/v1/zone/annually/1/1, sheet '人均&依存度&能源進口', Column5 = dependence on imported energy, Column9 = imported energy / energy supply.
- https://ea01.moeaea.gov.tw/a0303/02/api/v1/zone/annually/2/1 (supply by indigenous/imported, ktoe).

7) Statistics Canada WDS (check only)
POST https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/t1/wds/rest/getDataFromCubePidCoordAndLatestNPeriods with body [{"productId":36100711,"coordinate":"6.1.1.0.0.0.0.0.0.0","latestN":5}]
- Provinces only, no Canada total. Current dollars are null after 2022.
- Keep batches small: a 104-coordinate batch returned the maintenance page.

checks.measure: GDP (current US$)
checks.second_source: BEA NIPA annual flat file, series A191RC (GDP, US$ m), file dated 29 Oct 2026, which includes the 30 Sep 2026 annual update: 29,380,991. IMF WEO DataMapper NGDPD: 29,381.025 bn.
checks.note: 2024. The reported figure is BEA's vintage from before the September 2026 update. WDI (updated 2026-10-08) and OECD T0101 still carry it. It is 0.28% below the current BEA value: a small gap, but the figure has been superseded. The US PPP row (equal to nominal GDP) and every US ratio that uses this denominator carry the same lag. Example: exports on the BEA basis are 3,219,262 / 29,380,991 = 10.96%, against 10.97% reported. BEA has already published 2025 GDP: 30,861,292 US$ m. Raw files for all checks: /home/john/Desktop/Unity/.why-2-build/research/global/size_structure_check/

checks.measure: GDP (current US$)
checks.second_source: OECD SDMX Table 0101 (DF_TABLE1_OUTPUT), B1GQ in USD at exchange rates: 18,743,802 US$ m, from NBS's preliminary 134,908.35 bn yuan. IMF WEO NGDPD: 18,928.994 bn.
checks.note: 2024. Within 0.08% of the OECD figure. WDI uses the revised 134,807 bn yuan (NY.GDP.MKTP.CN) at the market rate of 7.19749 yuan/US$. The IMF WEO is 1.05% higher. It converts about 134,818 bn yuan (PPPEX x PPPGDP) at an implied 7.122, the PBOC central parity. This is a difference in conversion convention, not an error. Do not mix IMF and WDI dollar values for China, for example when Taiwan comes from the IMF.

checks.measure: GDP (current US$)
checks.second_source: Eurostat nama_10_gdp B1GQ CP_MEUR EU27_2020 (updated 2026-10-22): EUR 18,131,204.8 m, converted at the ECB 2024 average of 1.0824 US$/EUR (ert_bil_eur_a). IMF WEO 'EU': 19,592.298 bn.
checks.note: 2024. The WDI EUU aggregate is 0.63% below Eurostat's current figure and 0.47% below the IMF. It still holds member GDPs from before their revisions. Germany alone accounts for about +EUR 58 bn, roughly half the US$124 bn gap. The same dataset divides the extra-EU flows by Eurostat's EUR 18,131,204.8 m, so the bloc's GDP appears in two vintages. Use about US$19.63 trn for consistency.

checks.measure: GDP (current US$)
checks.second_source: Eurostat nama_10_gdp B1GQ CP_MEUR DE (provisional, updated 2026-10-22): EUR 4,386,940 m x 1.0824. OECD T0101: 4,748,338 US$ m. IMF WEO: 4,746.909 bn.
checks.note: 2024. The reported figure is stale. WDI's euro GDP (NY.GDP.MKTP.CN, EUR 4,328.97 bn) predates Destatis' revision to EUR 4,386.94 bn (+1.34%). All three current sources give about US$4.75 trn, so the reported value is 1.32% low. Germany's ratios shift a little: SIPRI military spending of EUR 79.59 bn is 1.81% of the revised GDP, against 1.84% reported.

checks.measure: GDP, PPP (current international $)
checks.second_source: IMF WEO DataMapper PPPGDP (current international $, bn): 38,289.661
checks.note: 2024. The two differ by 0.13%. Both rest on the ICP 2021 benchmark. The IMF confirms China's PPP GDP is above the US (38.29 vs 29.38 trn). The IMF's population figures (year-end 1,409.67 m in 2023 and 1,408.28 m in 2024) average exactly to WDI's 1,408.975 m. WDI and IMF PPP levels differ more for other economies: DEU 6,177 vs 6,081 bn, EU 28,728 vs 28,345 bn, IND 15,552 vs 15,680 bn.

checks.measure: Military expenditure (current US$)
checks.second_source: SIPRI Military Expenditure Database 1949-2025 (April 2026 workbook), sheet 'Current US$': USA 2024 = 1,004,901 US$ m. Independent brackets: NATO 2024e 935,000 US$ m (Table 2, Defence Expenditure of NATO Countries 2014-2025) and BEA NIPA national defense consumption + gross investment (A824RC) 1,073,539 US$ m.
checks.note: FY2024 (Oct 2023 to Sep 2024). Exact match with SIPRI, which WDI republishes. SIPRI footnote 44 confirms the fiscal-year basis. It also says the 2022-2024 US figures include SIPRI estimates of military aid to Ukraine and part of the National Intelligence Program. That is why the series falls to 954,387 US$ m in 2025. It is also why NATO's narrower 2024 estimate is 7% lower (3.21% of GDP, against SIPRI's 3.43%). BEA's calendar-year NIPA concept is 6.8% higher.

checks.measure: Military expenditure (current US$)
checks.second_source: SIPRI Milex 1949-2025, 'Current US$': CHN 2024 = 311,900.35 US$ m (2,244.9 bn yuan at 7.1975). Official budget for comparison: 1.69 trn yuan nationally, 1.67 trn central-level (NPC spokesperson as reported by Defence Connect, 13 Mar 2024).
checks.note: 2024. Exact match. The SIPRI estimate is 1.33 times the official national defence budget (1.69 trn yuan, about US$234.8 bn at 7.1975), which supports the row's note. The figure uses the market rate; at the IMF's central-parity rate it would be about US$315 bn. SIPRI's 2025 value is 335,524 US$ m.

checks.measure: Military expenditure (current US$)
checks.second_source: SIPRI Milex 1949-2025, 'Current US$' and 'Local currency calendar years': 13,827.502 bn roubles
checks.note: 2024. Exact match. Internally consistent: 13,827.5 bn RUB / 92.5524 RUB per US$ (WDI 2024 average) = US$149.40 bn. This is a SIPRI estimate, and I found no reliable second official source for the 2024 outturn. SIPRI's 2025 value is 190,417 US$ m.

checks.measure: Military expenditure
checks.second_source: Recomputed: SIPRI 13,827.502 bn RUB / Rosstat GDP 202,320 bn RUB as now carried by WDI NY.GDP.MKTP.CN. SIPRI's 'Share of GDP' sheet gives 6.8742% exactly.
checks.note: 2024, % of GDP. The SIPRI share implies an older GDP of about 201.15 trn RUB. Against the revised 202.32 trn the ratio is 6.83%, a 0.04 pp gap. SIPRI's 2025 share is 7.50%.

checks.measure: Military expenditure (current US$)
checks.second_source: European Defence Agency, Defence Data 2024-2025 (news, 2 Sep 2025): spending by the 27 member states was EUR 343 bn, 1.9% of GDP, converted at ECB 1.0824. Re-summing the 27 members in SIPRI's workbook gives 360,219.1 US$ m.
checks.note: 2024. The SIPRI member sum matches the reported value exactly (France 63,575, Germany 86,148, Italy 37,850, Poland 34,460 US$ m, and so on). The EDA figure follows national reporting and is about 3% higher. Both put the EU at roughly 1.8-1.9% of GDP. On Eurostat GDP the SIPRI sum is 1.835%, against 1.847% reported on WDI GDP.

checks.measure: Labor force, total
checks.second_source: BLS Current Population Survey, civilian labor force aged 16+ (LNU01000000), 2024 annual average (M13): 168,106 thousand
checks.note: 2024. The ILO modelled estimate is 6.06 m (3.6%) above the official BLS figure. Differences in concept explain part of the gap but not all of it. ILO counts ages 15+, includes about 1.3 m armed forces and benchmarks to UN WPP population. BLS counts the civilian non-institutional population aged 16+. Use BLS for the US, or label the row as an ILO model. Population (340,003,797 on 1 Jul 2024) matches Census Vintage 2025 exactly (NST-EST2025-POPCHG2020-2025.csv).

checks.measure: Manufacturing value added
checks.second_source: BEA GDP by Industry, Value Added by Industry (TVA105-A, published 30 Sep 2026): manufacturing 2,882,537 / GDP 29,380,991 US$ m. BEA's own TVA110-A rounds this to 9.8%.
checks.note: 2024. Within 0.07 pp. The reported value uses OECD T0101 at basic prices on the BEA vintage from before the update, which the OECD still serves. Price basis matters for the other US rows. On BEA's basis (value added including taxes on production less subsidies, summing to GDP), agriculture is 0.84% (0.94% reported), industry including construction 17.30% (17.34%), and services including government 83.48% (78.27%). The reported shares sum to 96.55% because product taxes are left out.

problems: Stale national-accounts vintages: several 2024 GDP values come from WDI (updated 2026-10-08), which lags national revisions. USA: 29,298.0 bn against BEA's current 29,381.0 bn (-0.28%, 30 Sep 2026 annual update). Germany: 4,685.6 bn against 4,748.4 bn (-1.32%; Destatis/Eurostat EUR 4,386.94 bn against WDI's EUR 4,328.97 bn). United Kingdom: 3,695.5 bn against 3,712.8 bn (OECD) and 3,713.6 bn (IMF) (-0.47%). EU27: 19,501 bn against 19,625 bn from Eurostat x ECB (-0.63%). The US PPP row and every share built on these GDPs inherit the lag.

US sector shares come from OECD T0101. That table still holds BEA's vintage from before the update (GDP 29,298,010) and uses basic prices: the shares sum to 96.55% and leave out about US$1.0 trn of net product taxes. BEA's 30 Sep 2026 tables give manufacturing 9.81%, agriculture 0.84% (0.94% reported) and services including government 83.5% (78.3% reported). The unit label should state both the price basis and the vintage.

China's GDP in dollars depends on the conversion. WDI and OECD use the 2024 market average of 7.1975 yuan/US$ (US$18.73-18.74 trn). IMF WEO uses the central parity of about 7.122 (US$18.93 trn, +1.05%). Any IMF-sourced row, such as Taiwan, must not be ranked against WDI China without saying which rate was used.

US labor force: the ILO modelled estimate (174.17 m) is 3.6% above the official BLS 2024 average (168.106 m, civilian, aged 16+). The other economies' ILO modelled labor forces may differ similarly from national surveys.

The note on US military spending is incomplete. SIPRI's 2024 US figure (US$1,004.9 bn) includes estimated military aid to Ukraine (2022-2024) and part of the intelligence budget (SIPRI footnote 44). That is why it falls to US$954.4 bn in 2025. NATO's 2024 estimate is US$935.0 bn (3.21% of GDP).

Coverage gap: the reported rows stop at Mexico's industry share. There are no rows for South Korea, Taiwan, Saudi Arabia or Brazil, none for Mexico's other measures, and no World row, although all were requested. Values I fetched for the gap: IMF WEO 2024 GDP KOR 1,880.8 bn, TWN 801.5 bn (PPP 1,884.0 bn; population 23.40 m), SAU 1,254.1 bn, BRA 2,185.8 bn. If Mexico's military row is added, check it first. SIPRI shows 20,595 US$ m (1.13% of GDP) for 2024, against 11,846 for 2023 and 13,648 for 2025, and its workbook has no footnote explaining the jump.

All natural-resource rent values are for 2021; the WDI series ends there (the re-fetch shows 2022-2025 empty). They reflect 2021 commodity prices, for example Russia 18.5% and Saudi Arabia 25.6% of GDP. Do not present them next to 2024 shares without a caveat.

A newer complete year exists. WDI (2026-10-08), BEA, IMF WEO, SIPRI (April 2026) and Eurostat already publish full-year 2025: US GDP US$30.86 trn, extra-EU exports EUR 4,255.3 bn, SIPRI military spending for 2025. 2024 follows the brief, but the rows should not imply it is the latest year available.

Mixed GDP bases for the EU bloc: the dataset carries WDI's EUU GDP (US$19.50 trn) next to extra-EU shares computed on Eurostat GDP (EUR 18.13 trn, about US$19.63 trn). On the WDI denominator, extra-EU exports would be 23.2% of GDP rather than 23.07%. Pick one EU GDP.
PPP levels from WDI and IMF differ by up to about 1.6% (DEU 6,177 vs 6,081 bn; EU 28,728 vs 28,345 bn; IND 15,552 vs 15,680 bn). A PPP ranking should take every economy from a single source.

title: The trade matrix between the economies

research.summary:
I built the matrix for 2024, as instructed. Data for 2025 also exist now; they appear only in the US-China mirror rows and in this summary. Raw downloads are in /home/john/Desktop/Unity/.why-2-build/research/global/trade-matrix/raw/. All rows are in trade_matrix_rows.json in the same folder, and scripts/build_rows.py rebuilds them offline.

WHAT THE ROWS ARE
- goods_exports 2024: all 14x13 reporter-partner pairs.
  - 12 reporters come from IMF IMTS (formerly DOTS; api.imf.org SDMX, updated 2026-10-31).
  - USA comes from the US Census country pages. These include the June revision; IMF's unrevised value is given in a note when it differs by more than 0.3%.
  - TWN comes from the Taiwan Ministry of Finance (MOF) trade-by-country CSV. IMF has no Taiwan-reported data and the World Bank omits Taiwan. TWN->EU27 is the sum of the 27 member-state columns.
- Partner 'ROW' = world total minus the listed partners, computed. Germany is counted inside EU27; for EU27, intra-EU trade is also removed.
- Also included: total goods exports and imports, US imports by partner, China's imports from the US, mirror gaps, and US services by partner (BEA).
- Units are US$ million; the Eurostat rows are EUR million.

VALUATION AND PARTNER RULES
- Exports are valued f.o.b. (US: f.a.s.).
- Imports are c.i.f., except: US (customs value); CAN, MEX and BRA (f.o.b. as reported, because IMF's c.i.f. series for them is a 5-6% conversion); Russia totals (balance-of-payments basis).
- Imports are attributed by country of origin, exports by destination; Taiwan uses last known destination.

US-CHINA MIRROR (2024)
- China reports exports to the US of 525.2bn. The US reports imports from China of 440.3bn at customs value (462.6bn c.i.f., per Comtrade). The gap is 84.9bn, or 19.3% of the US figure.
- The US reports exports to China of 143.3bn; China records imports from the US of 165.4bn c.i.f.
- So the US-reported deficit is 297.0bn, while China's data show a 359.8bn surplus.
- In 2025 the gap widened to 112.4bn: 421.0bn by China's count vs 308.7bn by the US count (36.4%).
- The 2009 US-China JCCT reconciliation explained the gap by three things: indirect trade via Hong Kong and other intermediaries (imports by origin vs exports by last destination), markups on goods resold en route, and c.i.f./f.o.b. valuation. At that time US-recorded imports were the larger figure; the sign has since reversed.
- Taiwan: China records 217.9bn of imports from Taiwan, while Taiwan records 97.0bn of exports to mainland China plus 53.6bn to Hong Kong.

OTHER DISCREPANCIES
- Germany: IMF uses Eurostat's community concept, which gives Germany imports from China of 103.0bn. Comtrade, on Destatis's national concept, gives 179.4bn (the Rotterdam effect). Exports are unaffected.
- UK: IMF excludes non-monetary gold. UK->China is 21.4bn in IMF vs 47.3bn in Comtrade/HMRC, of which 29.4bn is gold (HS 7108).
- Saudi Arabia: Comtrade puts 223.4bn of 305.5bn in exports under 'Areas, nes', so its partner split differs sharply from IMF's.
- India's imports from China: 109.4bn in IMF vs 127.0bn in Comtrade.
- Mexico->Taiwan: 0.7bn in IMF vs 4.9bn in Comtrade.
- Russia has published no partner data since 2022 and is absent from Comtrade. IMF fills Russia's rows from partner records; its series is flagged only 'Mixed-type data'. IMF's 2024 import total (239.9bn) is far below the Bank of Russia balance-of-payments figure (301.5bn), so Russia's totals use the Bank of Russia and its ROW rows use IMF.

EU27
- IMF G998 is Eurostat data in US dollars: EU->US is 579.7bn, i.e. EUR 535.6bn x 1.082.
- IMF's EU world total includes intra-EU trade: 4,338.6bn of 7,085.5bn in exports.
- Extra-EU exports: EUR 2,593.5bn (Eurostat), US$2,796.0bn (Comtrade), or 2,746.9bn (IMF world minus intra-EU).

SERVICES (BEA, balance-of-payments basis, 2024)
- US services exports 1,156.7bn; imports 829.4bn.
- Partner values come from BEA's selected-countries file.
- Russia is not shown separately there. From the USTR Russia page I computed exports of 1.21bn and imports of 0.37bn.
- Large partners outside the list: Ireland (85.9bn exports / 31.9bn imports) and Switzerland (64.9bn / 36.4bn).

WHAT FAILED, AND THE FALLBACK USED
- The Census API now requires a key (it redirects to missing_key.html), so I parsed the Census HTML country pages instead.
- WITS has no 2024 data. Its 2023 data match IMF exports within about 2%; US imports in WITS are c.i.f.
- Comtrade preview: one period per call, no Russia or Taiwan reporters, and HTTP 429 when calls are too fast.
- Taiwan's customs portal and the MOF database timed out, so I used the MOF CSV.
- The BEA API requires a key, so I used BEA's xlsx files.
- The Bank of Russia English statistics page returned 404, so I used the Russian-language xlsx.

2025 VALUES (in this summary, not in rows)
- US imports: 308.7bn from China, 201.4bn from Taiwan.
- Taiwan exports: 640.0bn in total, 198.3bn to the US.

IMF IMTS (no key)
- Request: GET https://api.imf.org/external/sdmx/2.1/data/IMF.STA,IMTS/{REP}.XG_FOB_USD+MG_CIF_USD..A?startPeriod=2024&detail=dataonly with header 'Accept: application/vnd.sdmx.data+csv;version=1.0.0'.
- REP is one of USA, CHN, G998 (EU27), DEU, JPN, IND, GBR, RUS, CAN, MEX, KOR, SAU, BRA. TWN as a reporter returns no rows.
- Columns used: COUNTRY, INDICATOR, COUNTERPART_COUNTRY, TIME_PERIOD, OBS_VALUE. OBS_VALUE is in US dollars (units).
- Counterpart codes are ISO3, plus TWN, G998 (EU) and G001 (World).
- Imports as CAN, MEX and BRA report them: .../IMF.STA,IMTS/CAN+MEX+BRA.MG_FOB_USD..A?startPeriod=2024&detail=dataonly
- Whole matrix in one call: .../{E}.XG_FOB_USD+MG_CIF_USD.{E}+G001.A?startPeriod=2024&endPeriod=2025&detail=dataonly with E=USA+CHN+G998+DEU+JPN+IND+GBR+RUS+CAN+MEX+KOR+TWN+SAU+BRA.
- Code lists: /dataflow/IMF.STA/IMTS/latest?references=all (large; extract CL_IMTS_COUNTRY).

US Census (no key)
- Pages: https://www.census.gov/foreign-trade/balance/c{code}.html
- Codes: 5700 CHN, 0003 EU, 4280 DEU, 5880 JPN, 5330 IND, 4120 GBR, 4621 RUS, 1220 CAN, 2010 MEX, 5800 KOR, 5830 TWN, 5170 SAU, 3510 BRA, 0015 World NSA.
- Parsing: strip script and style blocks and tags, unescape, then match 'TOTAL (\d{4})' followed by three numbers: exports, imports, balance, in US$ million.
- api.census.gov/data/timeseries/intltrade now redirects to missing_key.html without a key.

Taiwan MOF (no key)
- Files: https://service.mof.gov.tw/public/data/statistic/trade/u2010ex.csv and u2010im.csv.
- Encoding Big5. First-column labels: 'YYYY年' for annual rows, 'YYYY年M月' for monthly. Values in thousand US$.
- Column names: 總計 (total), 美國 (USA), 中國大陸 (CHN), 香港 (HKG), 日本 (JPN), 韓國 (KOR), 德國 (DEU), 英國 (GBR), 印度 (IND), 俄羅斯 (RUS), 加拿大 (CAN), 墨西哥 (MEX), 沙烏地阿拉伯 (SAU), 巴西 (BRA).
- EU27 = sum of the 27 member-state columns. Headers carry the suffix '(千元)'.
- Annual totals are also in NETE11509.xlsx (https://www.mof.gov.tw/Eng/download/21851), sheet Trend.

The $200bn list did not rise to 25% on 2019-01-01: the increase was postponed (83 FR 65198) and took effect on 2019-05-10 (84 FR 20459). An 'in force' description also leaves out List 4A (15% from 2019-09-01, cut to 7.5% from 2020-02-14; 84 FR 43304, 84 FR 45821, 85 FR 3741) and the 2024 increases, including EVs to 100% (89 FR 76581).

IEEPA-on-China magnitude leaves out two orders: EO 14228 (signed 2025-03-03, 90 FR 11463) doubled the fentanyl duty to 20%, and EO 14357 (90 FR 50725) cut it back to 10% from 2025-11-10. The combined additional IEEPA rate was therefore 145% at its peak (125+20) and 30% from 2025-05-14, not 10%. 'China's reciprocal rate' should read 'the US reciprocal rate on Chinese goods'.

Learning Resources event names the replacement measure but not its size: Proclamation 11012 (91 FR 9339, signed 2026-02-20) imposed a 10% Section 122 surcharge on imports for 150 days from 2026-02-24. Without it, the event reads as if the extra tariffs went to zero.

The dataset mixes mirror statistics without saying so. Matrix rows use exporter records while the event passages use importer records for the same flows: CHN→USA is 525.2bn in the matrix against 440.3bn (US imports) in the IEEPA passage; CAN+MEX→USA is 947.8bn against 914.9bn in the USMCA passage; RUS→CHN is 112.1bn against 128.3bn (China's imports) in the sanctions passage; RUS→IND is 68.7bn against 65.7bn. Label each figure as exporter- or importer-reported so a chart does not show two values for one arrow.

EU27→DEU (971.4bn) is the largest cell in the matrix, and it is intra-EU, community-concept data that includes quasi-transit through Rotterdam and Antwerp (NL→DE 216.3bn, BE→DE 99.9bn). On the national concept the same flows sum to 856.9bn (UN Comtrade; NL 155.2bn, BE 57.7bn), and Germany records 934.7bn of imports from the EU. Mark it as intra-EU and do not add it to extra-EU flows when sizing the EU bloc.

The Russia row note 'IMF estimate from partner records' is not supported. IMF flags every annual IMTS value as 'M' (mixed raw and derived data), for China, Germany and Mexico as well as Russia. Russia's values also depart from partners' own records in both directions: RUS→USA 1.8bn against 3.0bn US-recorded imports (-40%), RUS→CHN 112.1bn against 129.9bn (-14%), and RUS→IND 68.7bn, which is above India's own c.i.f. imports of 65.7–67.2bn. Treat the Russia rows as approximate.

UK rows from IMF are on a different basis than HMRC/Comtrade: GBR→EU27 is 222.5bn in IMF against 208.6bn in Comtrade (+6.7%), and UK total exports are 464.4bn in IMF against 454.8bn in HMRC excluding HS 7108 gold. The GBR→CHN note does not add up: 47,253.3 minus 29,407.0 of gold is 17,846.3, not 21,358.8. So 'IMF excludes gold' explains most of the gap but leaves 3.5bn (about 20%) unexplained.
MEX→USA and the 83.0% share depend on the source. IMF is 1.85% above Mexico's own Comtrade submission (503.4bn), which gives a share of 81.2%.

The data are stale as a picture of today. Every row is 2024, while full 2025 data are now published in IMF IMTS, Census, Eurostat, Taiwan MOF and China's Comtrade submission, and 2025 reordered key flows: TWN→USA rose from 111.4 to 198.3bn (+78%; Census imports from Taiwan 116.3 to 201.4bn), CHN→USA fell from 525.2 to 421.0bn, MEX→USA rose from 512.7 to 552.0bn, EU27→USA rose from 579.7 to 623.6bn, and CAN→USA fell from 435.1 to 403.9bn. If the matrix stays at 2024, label it '2024, before the 2025 tariff shock'.

Census figures are a later vintage than IMF's copies: 2024 US imports are 503,110.1 from Mexico (IMF 505,850.6), 411,771.6 from Canada (412,695.7) and 440,319.4 from China (438,947.4). Note the retrieval date (2026-11-03) and use one vintage throughout.

title: Conflict and coercion between the economies

research.summary:
I built 47 events and 130 measured rows on conflict and coercion between the listed economies, covering 2018 to November 2026. Raw downloads (184 small files, 11 MB) are in /home/john/Desktop/Unity/.why-2-build/research/global/conflict-coercion/raw/. The parsing scripts are in .../conflict-coercion/scripts/: fetch.sh, text.py, sent.py, census_totals.py, jsonstat.py, xlsx.py, piie_timeline.py and fr_docs.sh. Nothing was written inside the why-2 repository, and no credentials were used.

Main findings:
(1) US-China tariffs, from the PIIE chart data updated 22 Aug 2026. The average US tariff on Chinese goods was 3.1% in Jan 2018 and 19.3% from Feb 2020, covering 66.6% of imports (about $335bn). China's average on US goods went from 8.0% to 21%, covering 58.3%. In 2025 the US average peaked at 126.1% (3 May) and China's at 147.6% (12 Apr). After the Geneva truce (14 May 2025) they were 51.7% and 32.6%; from 10 Nov 2025, 47.4% and 31.9%. After the 20 Feb 2026 Supreme Court ruling ended the IEEPA tariffs, the US average fell to 31.2%. The Section 122 surcharge took it to 36.8% (24 Feb 2026), and the Section 301 forced-labor tariffs (from 24 Jul 2026) to 35.2% on 22 Aug 2026. The US average on all other countries went from 3.0% (20 Jan 2025) to 18.9% just before the ruling, and was 16.3% on 22 Aug 2026. Census: US imports from China fell from $440.3bn (2024) to $308.7bn (2025).
(2) 2026 developments, all after my training cutoff, verified in the Federal Register, USTR, PIIE and EIA:
- The Supreme Court ended the IEEPA tariffs on 20 Feb 2026.
- A 10% Section 122 surcharge ran from 24 Feb to 24 Jul 2026 (10%, not the 15% some reports said).
- Section 301 forced-labor tariffs on 60 economies started 24 Jul 2026: 10% for CAN, MEX, IND and GBR; 10% all-in for EU27 and TWN; 12.5% all-in for JPN and KOR; 12.5% for the rest, including CHN, BRA, SAU and RUS.
- Brazil got a separate 25% Section 301 tariff from 22 Jul 2026.
- Section 338 tariffs of 50% hit C$27.6bn of Canadian goods from 22 Aug 2026; Canada matched them from 8 Sep 2026.
- The US declined to renew the USMCA at its 1 Jul 2026 joint review.
- The US-India deal of Feb 2026 set an 18% tariff and ended the 25% Russian-oil penalty.
- The Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act order (Oct 2026) sets a 500% tariff on Russian goods and 100% secondary tariffs, all waived indefinitely.
- A US/Israel-Iran war began 28 Feb 2026 and closed the Strait of Hormuz. EIA: Brent rose from $71 to $104; Gulf producers shut in 7.5 mb/d in March, peaking at 10.9 mb/d in May; Brent averaged $114 in Sep 2026 and hit $131 after attacks on Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline.
(3) Measured magnitudes:
- Chips: US exports to China of chip-making machines (HS 8486) fell from $6.81bn (2021) to $2.28bn (2025) (Comtrade).
- China's mineral controls: China produces 99% of primary gallium and 82% of natural graphite. Its germanium metal exports for Jan-Sep fell from 36,656 kg (2023) to 7,520 kg (2025) (USGS).
- Russia trade: EU imports from Russia fell from €163.6bn (2021) to €27.9bn (2025) (Eurostat). US imports fell from $29.6bn to $3.0bn (Census). Russia's share of EU gas imports fell from 40.9% to 11.4%.
- Russian assets: Euroclear holds €200bn of sanctioned Russian assets (Mar 2026). The oil price cap went from $60 to $47.60 to $44.10.
- War deaths: OHCHR counts 16,874 civilians killed in Ukraine through Jul 2026.
- Red Sea: Suez tonnage fell 70% by mid-2024 (UNCTAD).
- Alliances: NATO 2025e defence spending was 3.22% of GDP for the US, 2.40% for the UK and 2.01% for Canada; Germany 2.00% in 2024. 60.9% of EU members' exports went to other EU members (2024). On IMF data, BRICS is 38.7% of world GDP at purchasing-power parity (40.0% with Saudi Arabia), the Quad 27.1% and USMCA 17.8% (2024).
- Other bilateral fights: Japan's hydrogen fluoride exports to Korea fell from $67.9m to $12.0m (2018 to 2020). China's imports of Japanese seafood fell from $507m to $0.1m (2022 to 2024). China's imports of Canadian canola seed fell from $3.29bn to $1.29bn (2024 to 2025).

Failures and substitutes:
- The Census trade API now needs a key; I used the public Census country pages instead.
- The IMF PortWatch daily chokepoint data now needs a token (499/403); I used UNCTAD and EIA passages instead.
- These sites block scripts: Council of the EU (403 browser check), EUR-Lex (202 empty), IEA (403), METI (403) and the IMF blog (403). I substituted the Commission press-corner API, the Commission finance directorate (DG FISMA), the EEAS, the WTO dispute page for Korea-Japan, and EIA for the IEA.
- NATO's 2026 spending report is image-only, so I used the 2025 report.
- The 2025 reciprocal-tariff Annex in the Federal Register text is an image, so I read the rates from the White House Annex PDFs.

Caveats:

events.name: US-China Section 301 tariff war, rounds 1-4A, and Chinese retaliation
events.end: ongoing (List 4A cut to 7.5% on 2020-02-14; tariffs still in force, raised on EVs/chips Sep 2024)
events.magnitude: Average US tariff on Chinese goods 3.1% (Jan 2018) to 19.3% (Feb 2020), covering 66.6% of US imports from China (about $335bn of 2017 trade). China's average on US goods 8.0% to 21%, covering 58.3% (about $90bn). Rounds: 25% on $34bn (6 Jul 2018), 25% on $16bn (23 Aug 2018), 10% on $200bn (24 Sep 2018, 25% from 2019), 15% on List 4A (1 Sep 2019).
events.source: PIIE (Bown) chart; USTR notices 83 FR 28710, 83 FR 47974, 84 FR 20459, 84 FR 43304, 85 FR 3741
events.passage: US tariffs on Chinese exports in February 2020 averaged 19.3 percent, more than six times higher than in January 2018. Those tariffs covered 66.6 percent of US imports from China, or roughly $335 billion of trade (measured in terms of 2017 import levels). Average Chinese tariffs on US exports starting in February 2020 were also at elevated levels of 21 percent, up from 8.0 percent prior to the trade war. China's retaliatory tariffs at the time covered 58.3 percent of imports from the United States, worth roughly $90 billion.

events.passage: Nevertheless, China did not live up to the commitment of purchasing an additional $200 billion of US goods and services over 2020 and 2021, as established by the legal agreement signed on January 15, 2020.

research.fetch_recipe:
All downloads are in /home/john/Desktop/Unity/.why-2-build/research/global/conflict-coercion/raw. Helper scripts are in .../scripts:
- fetch.sh: curl with a browser user agent.
- text.py and sent.py: HTML/PDF to text and sentence grep.
- census_totals.py, jsonstat.py, xlsx.py (stdlib xlsx reader), piie_timeline.py.
- fr_docs.sh: Federal Register metadata plus raw text.
Run Python with python3 -I. No keys are needed for any source.

1. US bilateral goods trade: the Census API now needs a key, so use the public country pages https://www.census.gov/foreign-trade/balance/c{CODE}.html. Codes: 5700 CHN, 1220 CAN, 2010 MEX, 0003 EU, 5880 JPN, 5330 IND, 3510 BRA, 5800 KOR, 5830 TWN, 4120 GBR, 4280 DEU, 4621 RUS, 5170 SAU, 5070 IRN. Send 'Accept: text/html'. Parse the rows 'TOTAL YYYY' followed by exports, imports and balance (USD million); census_totals.py does this.

2. PIIE US-China tariffs: the workbook https://www.piie.com/sites/default/files/2023-04/us-china-trade-war-tariffs.xlsx. Sheet 'Panel a' holds the action label, an Excel serial date (base 1899-12-30) and four average tariffs. Sheet 'Panel b' holds coverage. The narrative is on https://www.piie.com/research/piie-charts/2019/us-china-trade-war-tariffs-date-chart.

3. PIIE 'Trump's trade war timeline 2.0': take the Datawrapper iframe in the page (currently https://datawrapper.dwcdn.net/NaAq8/142/). The version number rises with each update, so read it from the page, then append /dataset.csv. The first-term timeline is in Google Sheets exported with https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/{id}/export?format=csv; the ids are in the knightlab iframes of the 2018 timeline page.

4. Federal Register: https://www.federalregister.gov/api/v1/documents/{docnum}.json gives raw_text_url. Searches use https://www.federalregister.gov/api/v1/documents.json?conditions[agencies][]=...&conditions[term]=...&conditions[publication_date][gte]=... and need curl -g. Key documents: 2025-02406/07/08, 2025-03775, 2025-06462, 2025-09297, 2025-14896, 2025-14999, 2025-15010, 2025-15267, 2025-15554, 2025-17389, 2025-19825/26, 2025-21417, 2025-10524, 2025-05930, 2026-01052, 2026-02813, 2026-02818, 2026-03824, 2026-03832, 2026-14991/92/97, 2026-15274, 2026-17294, 2026-21599, 2019-22056. BIS rules: 2022-21658, 2023-23049/55, 2024-28267/70, 2025-00636, 2025-19001, 2025-19846, 2026-00789. Reciprocal-rate annexes are images in the FR text; read them from the White House PDFs: https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/Annex-I.pdf and https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/2025ReciprocalTariffs_7.31.eo_.pdf (with pdftotext -layout, read the rate under each HTSUS 9903.02.xx heading).

5. UN Comtrade public preview: https://comtradeapi.un.org/public/v1/preview/C/A/HS?reporterCode=..&period=YYYY&partnerCode=..&cmdCode=..&flowCode=X|M&includeDesc=true. Only one period per call, about 1 call per second (HTTP 429 otherwise). Keep rows with motCode=0, partner2Code=0, customsCode=C00; the value is in primaryValue (USD). Codes: USA 842, CHN 156, JPN 392, KOR 410, CAN 124, RUS 643.

6. Eurostat JSON-stat at https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/api/dissemination/statistics/1.0/data/{dataset}?format=JSON&...
- ext_st_eu27_2020sitc is monthly (freq=M, indic_et=TRD_VAL, sitc06=TOTAL, partner RU/IR/CN_X_HK/US/EXT_EU27_2020). Sum 12 months; jsonstat.py does this.
- ext_lt_intratrd gives annual intra/extra shares.
- nrg_ti_gas gives gas imports by partner (siec G3000, unit MIO_M3).

7. USGS: https://pubs.usgs.gov/periodicals/mcs2026/mcs2026-{gallium|germanium|graphite|rare-earths|antimony}.pdf, read with pdftotext.

8. IMF WEO: https://www.imf.org/external/datamapper/api/v1/PPPSH and /NGDPD. Use a plain non-browser user agent; the indicators metadata endpoint is blocked. Sum member countries for 2024.

9. EIA:
- STEO: https://www.eia.gov/outlooks/steo/report/global_oil.php (current) and https://www.eia.gov/outlooks/steo/archives/{Mar26|Apr26|apr20}.pdf.
- Brent monthly: https://www.eia.gov/dnav/pet/hist/LeafHandler.ashx?n=PET&s=RBRTE&f=M.

10. Other single pages:
- European Commission press-corner JSON API: https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/api/documents?reference=IP/24/5589&language=en.
- DG FISMA price-cap page; EEAS copy of the European Council conclusions.
- Euroclear results (host cf.euroclear.com; www returns 403).

- NATO: Hague declaration and def-exp-2025-en.pdf (Table 3). The 2026 PDF is image-only.
- USTR USMCA statement; Treasury sm541; UNCTAD RMT 2024 page; WTO DS590 page.
- Canada Finance and PMO pages; MOFCOM English spokesperson pages and Chinese announcement pages.

research.summary:
Who finances whom, as of 3 Nov 2026.

(1) TIC (release of 16 Oct 2026, data to Aug 2026). Foreign holdings of US Treasuries were $9,331.7B at end-Aug 2026, against $9,249.1B a year earlier. Foreign official holders had $3,755.6B, down from $3,919.8B. By holder: Japan $1,068.3B (from $1,183.9B), UK $1,009.5B (from $901.3B), China $590.7B (from $699.7B); the TIC memo line for the EU27 was $2,144.6B; Russia $0.025B.
- The old mfh.txt is frozen at Jan 2023 (kept as tic/mfh_stale_jan2023.txt). Table 5 is the current table.
- Germany, Mexico, Russia and the EU memo line are not in Table 5's top 20, so they come from SLT Table 3. Table 3 matches Table 5 within rounding for every economy checked.
- TIC attributes holdings to the custodian's country (Belgium/Euroclear, Luxembourg, UK, Switzerland, Cayman), so China's and other official holdings may be understated and UK/EU holdings overstated.
- Year coding for TIC rows: 2026 = end Aug 2026, 2025 = end Aug 2025. Table 1 (all US long-term securities) is the SLT monthly estimate.

(2) COFER (published 30 Sep 2026). The USD share of allocated reserves was 56.70% in 2026-Q2, 56.95% in 2025-Q2 and 58.41% in 2024-Q4 (year coding 2026/2025/2024).
- Since the 2025Q3 release the IMF imputes the currency of the formerly 'unallocated' reserves (10.58% of the total in 2026-Q2) and has revised the series back to 2000. These shares are therefore not comparable with shares published before that change.

(3) Current account. IMF WEO October 2026 covers the 13 national economies, including Taiwan.
- Cross-checked against World Bank WDI (updated 8 Oct 2026): within 0.15 pp of GDP everywhere except India, which WEO reports by fiscal year (Apr-Mar).
- 2024 is the preferred year; 2025 is also complete in this vintage and is given.
- EU27 as a bloc uses Eurostat's extra-EU balance (EUR 449.6B, 2.48% of GDP in 2024), converted to US$ at Eurostat's annual average rate.
- The WEO 'EU' figure is the plain sum of the 27 members' own balances (verified: 614.726 vs 614.724 US$B for 2024). It is 3.1% of GDP and appears only in the notes.

(4) Net international investment position (NIIP).
- Source: IMF IIP dataset (national submissions) for 12 economies; Taiwan from its central bank (CBC); EU27 only excluding reserve assets, because Eurostat publishes no EU27 total that includes reserves. Shares of GDP are computed with WEO GDP of the same year.
- US revision: BEA's annual update (24 Jun 2026) moved end-2025 from -$27.54T to -$21.87T. End-2024 had been -$26.54T in the 25 Mar 2026 release and is now -$22.13T. The causes were a new method for marking FDI in the US to market value and the 2022 benchmark survey. Older figures near -$26T are superseded; the latest is -$22.42T at end of 2026-Q2.
- The UK net position swings widely by quarter; see the row notes.

(5) BEA direct investment positions (historical cost), both directions, from the 21 Jul 2026 release: 2025 and revised 2024.
- Fault found: BEA's 'selected countries' sheets for investment into the US rotate the labels of Malaysia, New Zealand, Singapore and South Korea in 2021 and 2023-2025. Korea is printed as 1,153 and 598 US$M for 2024/2025.
- Korea's values ($90.4B and $95.2B) are taken from BEA's ultimate-beneficial-owner (UBO) table, which agrees with the selected-countries sheets for every other country checked.
- Russia's inbound position is not shown separately (null).
- The UBO-basis positions are in the kept UBO file but are not given as rows.

Failures and gaps:
- consilium.europa.eu and euroclear.com returned HTTP 403, so there is no source for the size of Russia's immobilized reserves; the event row says so.
- The BEA API needs a key and was not used; the public XLSX tables were.
- Eurostat's bop_eu6_a is not disseminated; bop_eu6_q (annual frequency) was used.
- The World Bank has no Taiwan and returns null for the EU current account.

research.fetch_recipe:
All endpoints are public and need no key; send a User-Agent.

TIC
- GET https://ticdata.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/tic/Documents/slt_table5.txt. Tab-separated. The 'Country' row lists 13 month columns (YYYY-MM, newest first). Values are US$ billions. Total rows: 'Grand Total', 'Of Which: Foreign Official'.
- slt_table3.txt (Treasury holdings, all countries) and slt_table1.txt (all US long-term securities), same folder. Tab-separated: 9 header lines, then country, country_code, date (YYYY-MM), then US$ millions columns. Read column 4: for_treas_pos in Table 3, for_lt_total_pos in Table 1. Memo rows: 'Memo: European Union', 'Memo: Euro Area'.
- Files are 0.5-1 MB; stream them and filter by name and date.
- mfh.txt is frozen at Jan 2023; do not use it.

COFER
- GET https://api.imf.org/external/sdmx/2.1/data/IMF.STA,COFER/G001....Q?startPeriod=2024-Q1 with header 'Accept: application/vnd.sdmx.data+csv;version=1.0.0'.
- Key order: COUNTRY.INDICATOR.FXR_CURRENCY.TYPE_OF_TRANSFORMATION.FREQUENCY.
- INDICATOR: AFXRA, TFXRA, TFXRA_IMP. FXR_CURRENCY: CI_USD, CI_EUR, CI_JPY, CI_GBP, CI_CNY, CI_T. TYPE: SHRO_PT (percent) or NV_USD (US$ units).
- Read TIME_PERIOD and OBS_VALUE. Each row carries about 2 KB of metadata, so keep only the needed columns.

WEO current account and GDP
- GET https://www.imf.org/external/datamapper/api/v1/{BCA|BCA_NGDPD|NGDPD}. Result: values[indicator][ISO3 or group][year].
- Country paths and ?periods are ignored; all countries come back.
- Groups: 'EU' (equals the sum of the 27 members) and 'EURO'. Taiwan is 'TWN'.
- Vintage is in https://www.imf.org/external/datamapper/api/v1/indicators ('World Economic Outlook (October 2026)').

World Bank cross-check
- https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/USA;CHN;EUU;DEU;JPN;IND;GBR;RUS;CAN;MEX;KOR;SAU;BRA;TWN/indicator/BN.CAB.XOKA.GD.ZS?format=json&date=2022:2025&per_page=500 (and the same for BN.CAB.XOKA.CD).
- No TWN; EUU returns null.

Net IIP (IMF)
- GET https://api.imf.org/external/sdmx/2.1/data/IMF.STA,IIP/USA+CHN+DEU+JPN+IND+GBR+RUS+CAN+MEX+KOR+SAU+BRA+G163.NETAL_P.NIIP.USD.A+Q?startPeriod=2023 with the same Accept header.
- OBS_VALUE is in US$ units. G163 is the euro area. There is no TWN or EU27.

Taiwan net IIP (CBC)
- Scrape https://www.cbc.gov.tw/en/cp-513-26934-DD294-2.html for the PDF (or XLSX/ODS) link. It is currently https://www.cbc.gov.tw/en/dl-171196-7e9b39e33fed4a039b72a6417772e74c.html; the dl- ids change with each release.
- Run pdftotext -layout and read the 'Net international investment position' line against the year header (2000 to latest; US$ millions).

Eurostat (JSON-stat)
- Base: https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/api/dissemination/statistics/1.0/data/
- bop_eu6_q?geo=EU27_2020&freq=A&sector10=S1&sectpart=S1&bop_item=CA&stk_flow=BAL&currency=MIO_EUR&partner=EXT_EU27_2020 (also partners US and CN_X_HK). Take s_adj=NSA.
- bop_iip6_q?geo=EU27_2020&partner=EXT_EU27_2020&bop_item=FA__TXR__F&sector10=S1&sectpart=S1&stk_flow=N_LE&currency=MIO_EUR&freq=A. Totals FA and FA__R__F are not published for EU27.
- nama_10_gdp?geo=EU27_2020&unit=CP_MEUR&na_item=B1GQ
- ert_bil_eur_a?currency=USD&statinfo=AVG&statinfo=END
- Decode the 'value' keys as row-major indexes over 'id' and 'size'.
- bop_eu6_a is not disseminated.

BEA direct investment
- GET https://apps.bea.gov/international/xls/usdia-current/usdia-positionbyaccountforselectedcountries-2020-2025.xlsx and https://apps.bea.gov/international/xls/fdius-current/fdius-position-selected-countries-2020-2025.xlsx. One sheet per year; column B is the total position in US$ millions; EU27 is the row 'European Union 3' under 'Addendum'.
- https://apps.bea.gov/international/xls/fdius-current/fdius-ubo-fp-country-2020-2025.xlsx: sheet '2020-2025', four columns per year (foreign-parent position, income, UBO position, income). Take South Korea's inbound position from this file, because the selected-countries sheets for 2021 and 2023-2025 rotate the labels of Malaysia, New Zealand, Singapore and South Korea.
- File names roll forward each July (…-2020-2026). The links are listed on https://www.bea.gov/news/2026/direct-investment-country-and-industry-2025.
- The apps.bea.gov/international/ index returns 403, but the files download.
- Parse XLSX with zipfile + xml.etree (no openpyxl needed). The BEA API needs a UserID and was not used.

BEA NIIP passages
- https://www.bea.gov/news/2026/us-international-transactions-and-investment-position-1st-quarter-2026-and-annual-update (revision) and https://www.bea.gov/news/2026/us-international-transactions-and-investment-position-2nd-quarter-2026 (latest).

Computed values
- EU27 % of GDP = balance / nama_10_gdp.
- EU27 in US$ = EUR value x ert_bil_eur_a (annual average for flows, end of year for positions).
- Net IIP % of GDP = IMF IIP (or CBC) value / WEO NGDPD of the same year.

problems: NIIP as a share of GDP is wrong for most rows in a currency other than the dollar. Each ratio divides a stock converted at the year-end exchange rate by GDP converted at the average rate (WEO NGDPD). With IMF end-of-period and period-average rates (IMF.STA,ER), the ratios computed consistently in national currency are: DEU 78.7 / 80.9 (reported 75.5 / 84.1; Eurostat publishes 78.6 / 80.8); JPN 84.5 / 84.3 (reported 81.6 / 80.7); KOR 2024 62.3 (reported 57.8); BRA 2024 -43.9 (reported -38.2); RUS 47.7 / 39.9 (reported 43.4 / 42.6); MEX -34.5 / -31.6 (reported -31.1 / -33.8, so the direction of change is reversed); CAN 64.8 / 51.5 (reported 61.8 / 52.5). USA, SAU (dollar peg), CHN and GBR are within about 0.5 pp. Fix: compute in national currency, or divide by GDP converted at the year-end rate.

China's current account (WEO Oct 2026) is one revision behind. SAFE's time series dated 29 Sep 2026 has 2025 = US$735.0 bn and 2024 = 462.3 bn, against the reported 724.4 and 458.5. WDI already uses SAFE's figures. The share of GDP is unchanged once rounded (about 3.7%).

The US NIIP values are correct for the current vintage, but they come after a break in method. BEA's annual update of 24 Jun 2026 revised end-2025 from -$27.54T to -$21.87T (liabilities from 70.49T to 64.78T) and end-2024 from -$26.54T to -$22.13T. BEA now revalues foreign direct investment equity in the US at market value and has added its 2022 benchmark survey. Do not compare with pre-June-2026 figures or with familiar values near -90% of GDP. The real 2024-25 change is small (+$0.25T).

COFER vintage: since the 2025-Q3 release the IMF imputes the currency composition of non-reporting holders. Unallocated reserves are now zero in every period, so 'allocated' equals total, and the 2024-Q4 share of 58.41% is on the new basis. It is not comparable with shares published before that change. The year series also mixes quarters (2024-Q4 vs 2025-Q2 and 2026-Q2). For an end-year series, use 2025-Q4 = 56.52%.

Gap: Taiwan has no NIIP row (the IMF IIP query omitted TWN). The CBC release of 15 Jun 2026 reports end-2025 net external assets of US$1,349.6 bn and ranks Taiwan the 6th largest net creditor, larger than Russia (1,096.9), Saudi Arabia (722.8) or Korea (885.7).

The size of the sanction on the Central Bank of Russia was left null, although a sourced figure exists. EPRS (Feb 2024) gives US$300 bn frozen across jurisdictions. Most is held in the EU, mainly at Euroclear; the EU and Euroclear pages are blocked (403), so the EU share of about EUR 210 bn is unverified. The US-held part is small, so the event's party framing ('USA ... against RUS') understates the coordinated scope.

US–Japan: 'the US to retain 90% of the profits' quotes the fact sheet of 23 Jul 2025 correctly, but it may be stale. The implementing MOU of 4 Sep 2025 reportedly splits cash flows 50/50 until Japan's contribution is recouped, then 90/10. I could not verify this: commerce.gov and mofa.go.jp returned 403. Flag it before publishing the 90% figure as the deal's terms.
US–Korea: the cap of US$20 bn per calendar year applies to the dollar funding of the US$200 bn MOU (strategic investments), not to the whole US$350 bn package.

Unverified outlier in the notes: the IMF IIP series shows Korea's NIIP falling from 753.6 (2026-Q1) to 64.0 (2026-Q2), a drop of about $690 bn in one quarter. I could not cross-check it with the Bank of Korea because its site renders by JavaScript. Treat it as provisional.

The custodial caveat in TIC applies to every country row, not only GBR, CHN and EU27. Belgium (490.5), Luxembourg (448.2), Cayman Islands (463.0) and Ireland (352.1) hold large custodial positions whose owners are attributed elsewhere. The long-term securities total (39,916.3) includes international organizations and excludes T-bills.
Not independently checkable here: the EU–US bilateral current-account mirror (BEA's figure for the US with the EU needs an API key), and UK figures (ONS returned 403).

title: Critical dependencies and chokepoints in the global value chain

research.summary:
Measured concentration of the inputs under the technology summit, with one row per economy and value (154 rows, 17 events). The full data with checked passages is at /home/john/Desktop/Unity/.why-2-build/research/global/chokepoints/chokepoints_compact.json. A longer-note version is chokepoints_rows.json in the same folder. Raw downloads are under raw/ and the scripts under scripts/. The build script build_compact.py checks that every quoted table row or sentence appears in the saved source text.

KEY FINDINGS
- Advanced logic below 10 nm (SIA/BCG 2024, Exhibit 6, 2022 capacity): Taiwan 69%, Korea 31%, everyone else 0%. The US is 0% ('did not produce any advanced logic chips'). The 2032 forecast is Taiwan 47, US 28, Korea 9, Europe 6, Japan 5, China 2. The earlier SIA/BCG 2021 report gave Taiwan 92%, Korea 8% for 2019. The bar colours were read from a rendered crop of the chart because the PDF text order is ambiguous.
- Rare earths (USGS MCS 2026, revised 2024): China 71.1% of mine output (270,000 of 380,000 t REO), US 12.0%. The IEA gives China 91% of magnet rare-earth refining in 2024.
- Gallium: China 98.9% of primary output (839 of 848 t, 2024).
- Germanium: USGS publishes no country data. I used EU CRM 2023, which gives a 2016-2020 average: China 83.1%, Russia 5.0%, EU 7.2%, US 2.0%, Japan 1.8%.
- Lithium mine output (2024, world excluding the withheld US figure): China 18.6%. Refining (IEA 2024): China 70%, US 1%.
- Cobalt mine output: DR Congo 74.8%. China holds 78% of refining (IEA 2024).
- Crude oil production (EIA, 2024): US 16.2%, Russia 12.1%, Saudi Arabia 11.2%.
- Crude exports (Comtrade mirror, value basis, 2024): Saudi Arabia 14.1%, Russia 9.4%, US 9.0%, Canada 8.5%.
- LNG exports (GIIGNL, 2024): US 21.0%, Qatar 19.3%, Australia 19.5%, Russia 8.3%.
- Data-centre electricity (IEA, 2024): US 45%, China 25%, Europe 15%.
- AI supercomputer performance (Epoch, March 2025): US about 75%, China about 15%. Shares computed from Epoch's public file for end-2024 are also included.

NEW IN 2026 (from EIA)
- The Strait of Hormuz has been effectively closed since the conflict in Iran began on 28 February 2026. Middle East crude shut-ins peaked at 10.9 million b/d in May and were 4.8 million b/d in September. About 20% of world LNG supply was affected, and flows remain constrained through 4Q26.
- The UAE left OPEC on 1 May 2026.
- The US imposed a 25% Section 232 tariff on certain advanced chips from 15 January 2026.
- The US-China suspensions of tariffs and of China's mineral controls are scheduled to end on 10 November 2026.

WHAT FAILED AND WHAT REPLACED IT
- The Energy Institute Statistical Review, the OPEC Annual Statistical Bulletin and IEA HTML pages returned Cloudflare challenges (HTTP 403). I did not bypass them. I used IEA PDFs on the public iea.blob host instead.
- EIA's crude export series stops in 2018. JODI 2024 lacks Russia, the UAE, Iran and Brazil. So crude export shares are Comtrade mirror values: importers' CIF reports over $1,328.7 bn of world imports. These are value shares, not volumes, and Russian crude sold at a discount. Iranian crude is largely unrecorded by origin. The EU27 figure (1.95%) is mostly re-exports through the Netherlands.

CAVEATS
- Semiconductor figures are wafer capacity, not output. The 'Europe' region is used as the EU27 proxy for wafer capacity.
- For USGS minerals I used the MCS 2026 revised 2024 values rather than the MCS 2025 first estimates named in the task. The first estimates are kept in the notes; for rare earths they were China 69.2%, with large revisions for Australia, Nigeria and Thailand.
- The IEA refining figures give shares only for China, plus US lithium. The EU27 cobalt refining share (17%) is from EU CRM 2016-2020.
- IEA data-centre figures are modelled estimates. IEA 'Europe' is not the EU27, so EU27 is null and a separate EUROPE_IEA row is given.
- Epoch's dataset covers about 10-20% of AI supercomputers. Chinese entries in the public file are anonymized and rounded.
- Zeros are given only where the source table shows zero or lists all producers. Rows for economies a source does not list were omitted, not set to zero:
  - rare earths: EU27, DEU, JPN, GBR, MEX, KOR, TWN, SAU (at most 1,000 t in 'Other')
  - germanium: IND, GBR, CAN, MEX, KOR, TWN, SAU, BRA
  - cobalt mine output: EU27 (Finland), DEU, JPN, IND, GBR, MEX, KOR, TWN, SAU, BRA (within 'Other' 7,780 t)
  - data centres: DEU, GBR, RUS, CAN, MEX, KOR, TWN, SAU, BRA
- Context rows for economies outside the requested list show where the concentration sits: MMR, AUS, CHL, COD, IDN, QAT, IRQ, IRN, ARE. WLD rows hold world totals.

research.fetch_recipe:
None of these sources needs a key or an account. Raw copies and text extractions are under /home/john/Desktop/Unity/.why-2-build/research/global/chokepoints/raw and the scripts under ../scripts. Rebuild the rows with: python3 -I scripts/build_compact.py <dir>. It checks every quoted token against the saved text.

1. USGS MCS 2026 chapters: https://pubs.usgs.gov/periodicals/mcs2026/mcs2026-{rare-earths,gallium,germanium,lithium,cobalt}.pdf (mcs2025-*.pdf for first estimates). Run pdftotext -layout, read the 2024 column of 'World Mine Production and Reserves' (or 'World Low-Purity Production' for gallium), and divide each row by the World total.

2. EIA bulk file: https://www.eia.gov/opendata/bulk/INTL.zip (JSON lines, about 24 MB). Read series INTL.57-1-<ISO3>-TBPD.A and INTL.57-1-WORL-TBPD.A (crude incl. lease condensate, kb/d; the EU27 code is EU27). Scripts: eia_scan.py keep, then eia_shares.py.

3. UN Comtrade public preview: GET https://comtradeapi.un.org/public/v1/preview/C/A/HS?period=2024&cmdCode=2709&flowCode=M&partnerCode=<M49>. Sum primaryValue over reporters, excluding the partner itself, and divide by the same sum for partnerCode=0. Wait about 2 s between calls or it returns HTTP 429. Script: comtrade_crude.py.

4. GIIGNL: https://giignl-documents.s3.fr-par.scw.cloud/public/ar-2025-annual-report.pdf, table 'Source of LNG imports in 2024' (Mt).

5. SIA/BCG 2024 PDF, Exhibit 6 on page 14. The text order is ambiguous, so read the segment colours from a render: pdftoppm -f 14 -l 14. The order is US, Europe, Japan, Korea, Taiwan, China, Other. SIA/BCG 2021 is Exhibit 17.
